title: Euro 2012 Players to Watch: Manuel Neuer of Germany
content: Germany and Bayern Munich’s latest No. 1, Manuel Neuer, succeeded in proving his worth to the latter’s fans this past season. Neuer will be keen to play his part in ensuring the German national side go one better at Euro 2012. In keeping with the fortunes of a club who have not been able to add to their seven German championships since their last success in 1957-58, Neuer alone was unable to help bring the success Schalke fans crave, getting as close as runners-up in his inaugural Bundesliga season and again in 2009-10. One piece of silverware did arrive the following season in the form of the German Cup. Neuer was an ever-present, recording four clean sheets in six rounds (only conceding three goals), two of which came in the semifinals (a 1-0 win over Bayern) and in the 5-0 final demolition of MSV Duisburg. A major hint that his future may lie elsewhere of his hometown club came in the form of Neuer’s elevation to the Germany No. 1 spot.

title: Germany recall Manuel Neuer, 40, as first-choice goalkeeper - BBC
content: Neuer helped Germany win the 2014 World Cup. **Bayern Munich goalkeeper Manuel Neuer has come out of international retirement to be named in Germany's squad for the 2026 World Cup, with manager Julian Nagelsmann saying the 40-year-old will be his team's number one for the tournament.**. Neuer, who has helped Bayern win the Bundesliga title and reach the Champions League semi-finals this season, won the last of his 124 caps for his country in a Euro 2024 quarter-final defeat by Spain. Neuer has played in four World Cups and is the latest of a number of players aged 40 or over to be selected for this summer's tournament, which will take place across Canada, Mexico and the United States. Who are the oldest players to feature at a World Cup? Since winning the 2014 tournament, Germany have bowed out at the group stage of the 2018 and 2022 World Cups.

title: Manuel Neuer - Wikipedia
content: Neuer won the [Footballer of the Year](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Footballer_of_the_Year_(Germany) "Footballer of the Year (Germany)") prize,[[60]](#cite_note-Manuel_Neuer_named_German_Footballer_of_the_Year-61) was voted into the UEFA Team of the Year,[[61]](#cite_note-Bayern_dominate_UEFA_Team_of_the_Year_poll-62) and finished third in the [FIFA Ballon d'Or](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_FIFA_Ballon_d'Or "2014 FIFA Ballon d'Or").[[62]](#cite_note-Cristiano_Ronaldo_wins_Ballon_d’Or_over_Lionel_Messi_&_Manuel_Neuer-63) Neuer started the season by winning the [2014 DFL-Supercup](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_DFL-Supercup "2014 DFL-Supercup") against Borussia Dortmund.[[63]](#cite_note-:3-64) On 30 January 2015, Neuer started[[64]](#cite_note-65) on matchday 18, where Bayern lost to [VfL Wolfsburg](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/VfL_Wolfsburg "VfL Wolfsburg") 4–1.[[65]](#cite_note-Die_Bayern_kassieren_eine_krachende_Niederlage-66) This was the first league match since joining Bayern in 2011 where he had given up four goals in a match. Neuer's [2019–20](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019–20_FC_Bayern_Munich_season "2019–20 FC Bayern Munich season") started with a 2–0 loss to Borussia Dortmund in the [German Super Cup](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_DFL-Supercup "2019 DFL-Supercup") on 3 August 2019.[[86]](#cite_note-Sancho_glänzt_in_doppelter_Rolle:_BVB_gewinnt_Supercup-87) On 21 May 2020, Neuer signed a new contract with Bayern, keeping him at the club until 2023.[[87]](#cite_note-88) On 23 August, Neuer won the Champions League for the second time, his first as Bayern captain, keeping a clean sheet as his team won [1–0](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UEFA_Champions_League_Final "2020 UEFA Champions League Final") over [PSG](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris_Saint-Germain_F.C.
